Imran Khan’s sister Uzma, with his personal physician Faisal Sultan speaks to reporters in Islamabad, August 21, 2026 [Anjum Naveed/AP]

articles.title: Predicting AEW All In 2026 Surprises From Britt Baker's Return to New Day's Debut
articles.summary: All In has been AEW's premier pay-per-view event since its inception in 2023, and the upcoming installment has the potential to be equally exceptional with what's on tap.
articles.body:
All In has been AEW's premier pay-per-view event since its inception in 2023, and the upcoming installment has the potential to be equally exceptional with what's on tap.

Kenny Omega and Will Ospreay's highly anticipated main event, Willow Nightingale and Mercedes Moné's AEW Women's World Championship clash and the first-time encounter over the AEW World Tag Team Championship are all guaranteed to be great from an in-ring standpoint, but there are bound to be several surprises in store as well.

All In 2024 featured Nigel McGuinness' return to the ring in his native England and Ricochet's All Elite Wrestling debut, while the returns of Bryan Danielson and Darby Allin highlighted All In 2025, so a precedent has been set for milestone moments occurring at the annual event.

From unpredictable outcomes to new champions being crowned, these are six shockers that could feasibly transpire at All In 2026.

Britt Baker Returns in Women's Casino Gauntlet

It was at All In two years ago that Britt Baker, an AEW original, had her last major match in the promotion, unsuccessfully challenging Mercedes Moné for the AEW TBS Championship.

However, the battle between two of the bigger names in women's wrestling in the last decade fell well short of fans' expectations.

Baker only made a handful of appearances on AEW TV after that before disappearing entirely from programming in November 2024. Although Tony Khan has responded to inquiries regarding her absence on media conference calls since then, her status hasn't seemed to change.

Baker was brought back up again by fans recently when Fightful Select 's Sean Ross Sapp revealed in a Q&A that she was internally discussed for the upcoming Rebel tribute edition of Dynamite on Sept. 9 in Georgia. The two were synonymous with each other in AEW's first few years.

It would make sense to reintroduce her before then in the women's Casino Gauntlet match at All In, where the winner will earn a future shot at the AEW Women's World Championship she once held.

The wrestling dentist doesn't necessarily have to win, but it would be quite the surprise to see her again amid social media rumors that she's eyeing an exit from the company due to her inactivity.

Kevin Knight is scheduled to have his biggest bout yet at All In when he defends the AEW TNT Championship against Darby Allin in a Falls Count Anywhere match.

The reigning champ is in the middle of a career year, having held the title since early April and racking up the most successful defenses for the TNT title ever. He also headlined last month's Redemption event with AEW world champion Kenny Omega and looked credible in defeat.

He's been a member of The Don Callis Family since shortly after turning heel at Double or Nothing in May, the same show where he betrayed his buddy, Darby Allin. Seeds have been planted over the last month that this new sinister side of Knight isn't the real him and that he'll soon see the light once he's away from Callis.

Perhaps it's his obsession with the gold that has made him so arrogant, and once he loses it to Allin on AEW's biggest stage, he'll realize the error of his ways.

While such a significant development for his character would be premature at this stage, it isn't completely out of the question for Sunday's pay-per-view.

Nigel McGuinness Wins the AEW Continental Championship

The ongoing Continental Challenge Cup has been a unique way of determining what the AEW Continental Championship match will be at All In, and as of this writing, only four wrestlers remain.

It will be either Jon Moxley or Claudio Castagnoli taking on Kyle O'Reilly or Nigel McGuinness for the title.

As the defending champ, Moxley should walk into the event with the belt, and seeing as how he already beat O'Reilly to retain the title in May, the finals of the tournament should be Moxley vs. McGuinness at All In.

In such a situation, Moxley would be automatically expected to emerge victorious, which would make an upset from McGuinness all the more surprising.

As noted, it was at All In two years ago that he returned to the ring for the first time since 2011 in front of his countrymen at Wembley Stadium. It would be huge for him to be the one to end Moxley's lengthy title reign on that same show two years later.

McGuinness may not be a full-time member of the active roster anymore, but it would be a fitting final chapter to his career as well as a memorable moment for those in attendance.

The New Day Win the AEW World Trios Titles with Swerve Strickland

Kofi Kingston and Xavier Woods have been a hot topic of conversation among wrestling fans since receiving their release from WWE at the beginning of May.

They were always expected to have interest from AEW upon entering free agency, and now their debut may be imminent.

Swerve Strickland curiously teased challenging for the AEW World Trios Championship on a recent Dynamite. Since he doesn't currently have any established allies on the roster, it was safe for fans to assume that he could be enlisting the likes of the former New Day to go after the gold with him.

Kingston and Woods obviously belong in the tag team ranks, but there's nothing wrong with starting them out with Strickland to ensure them a spot on the show. Plus, Strickland and The New Day could turn out to be quite the formidable force.

The AEW World Trios title match for All In is not yet set in stone, but if it's some sort of multi-team affair featuring a variety of trios, look for Strickland and New Day to not only enter but also to leave as the new champions.

Willow Nightingale and Mercedes Moné are no strangers to each other. They've collided in both New Japan Pro-Wrestling and in AEW and have traded wins over the NJPW Strong Women's Championship and the AEW TBS Championship.

At All In, they'll meet one-on-one yet again, this time for the AEW Women's World Championship. Nightingale won the title for the first time only a month ago at Redemption, while Moné secured her shot by capturing the women's Owen Hart Cup two years in a row.

All signs point to the third time being the charm for Moné (after failing in her previous opportunities at All In 2025 and Full Gear 2025) and her taking the title that has eluded her since her arrival in the promotion, but Nightingale retaining would be the more interesting outcome.

Moné falling short would force her "crash out" to continue, and effectively turn Nightingale from a perennial chaser to a certified champion. Moné ended Nightingale's TBS title run after only one month, but history shouldn't repeat itself here.

Nightingale will again have Moné's number and pull out the win against the odds.

Sheamus, Ilja Dragunov Debut in the Men's Casino Gauntlet

The New Day may not be the only ones making their first-ever AEW appearance at All In this weekend at Wembley Stadium.

Two more familiar faces who recently left WWE on their own terms and are presumably exploring new ventures are Sheamus and Ilja Dragunov. Both men's contracts recently expired after not being featured on WWE TV for many months.

Sheamus and Dragunov were known for their intense, hard-hitting style during their time in WWE and would be perfect fits for the AEW landscape. If they are free and clear of any contractual obligation to WWE, why not have them show up during the men's Casino Gauntlet match at All In?

One of them alone would make an immediate impact, but putting them both in the same bout would be the bigger shocker of them all, similar to how Adam Cole and Bryan Danielson debuted in AEW within minutes of each other at All Out in 2021. They wouldn't be overshadowed provided they're in there for long enough and are allowed to have strong showings.

Sheamus and Dragunov being "All Elite" is inevitable, and there would be no better time or place for them to make their presence felt and potentially punch their ticket to AEW World Championship contention out of the gate.

Graham Mirmina, aka Graham "GSM" Matthews, has specialized in sports and entertainment writing since 2010. Visit his website, WrestleRant , and subscribe to his YouTube channel for more wrestling-related content.

articles.title: BS Meter on Dylan Larkin, Cutter Gauthier and the Latest NHL Trade Rumors
articles.summary: The dog days of the NHL off-season continue as August draws to a close.
articles.body:
The dog days of the NHL off-season continue as August draws to a close.

Following a frenzy of activity in the trade market within the first two days of July, business has slowed to a crawl. Only five trades have occurred since July 2 , all involving minor-league players.

However, trade activity could pick up once the calendar flips to September. With training camps opening in mid-month and the regular season beginning on Sept. 29 , NHL general managers could soon start shopping around to address any lingering roster issues.

Meanwhile, the media rumor mill continues churning over potential moves involving some key players.

Some, such as Detroit Red Wings center Dylan Larkin, have previously surfaced in trade rumors this summer. Others, like Calgary Flames defenseman Zach Whitecloud, have started popping up as trade candidates.

Follow along as we dust off our BS Meter to separate fact from fiction regarding the latest NHL trade chatter.

Montréal Canadiens Have 2 'Sign-and-Trade' Candidates

With September and the start of training camp fast approaching, the Montréal Canadiens have not yet re-signed defenseman Arber Xhekaj and winger Zachary Bolduc. The two depth players are restricted free agents coming off low-cost contracts and should be affordable re-signings for the Canadiens.

Stu Cowan of The Montreal Gazette speculated about whether Xhekaj and Bolduc still have futures with the Canadiens. Because they haven't re-signed yet, he concluded that they could be part of a sign-and-trade scenario.

The Canadiens still require a second-line center. Cowan pointed out that general manager Kent Hughes hasn't ruled out making a trade in September or October, adding that he wouldn't make a "dumb trade" for a quick fix.

Given the young talent within the Canadiens system, there might not be room for Xhekaj and Bolduc. They could be pushed out if one or two of their promising players crack the lineup during training camp.

Sign-and-trade scenarios usually happen with stars or second-tier talent, not low-cost depth players. Both could draw attention if available in the trade market. However, even in a package deal, they won't fetch the second-line center the Canadiens require without adding a significant sweetener.

Darcy Kuemper and Trevor Moore Could Be Los Angeles Kings' Trade Candidates

The Los Angeles Kings made several roster changes during this offseason.

Long-time captain Anze Kopitar retired, and Andrei Kuzmenko and Mathieu Joseph departed via free agency. Mats Zuccarello and Erik Haula arrived via free agency. So did Corey Perry, back for a second stint after joining them last season.

Nevertheless, Kings general manager Ken Holland might not be done tinkering with his lineup this season. Ryan O'Hara of The Hockey News suggested goaltender Darcy Kuemper and winger Trevor Moore as trade candidates .

Kuemper, 36, was a Vezina Trophy finalist with the Kings in 2024-25. However, he struggled last season after an injury, which cost him the starter's job to Anton Forsberg. If he can't regain that spot, the Kings might attempt to move him and his $5.3 million cap hit .

O'Hara complimented Moore's speed and ability, but noted the 31-year-old winger hasn't cracked the Kings' top-six forward lines full-time. He carries a $4.2 million annual cap hit through 2027-28 , and scored a career-high 31 goals in 2022-23.

Both players could be trade chips to address other roster issues for the Kings. Kuemper could draw interest from teams seeking an experienced starting goalie, while Moore could entice clubs that are in the market for a skillful middle-six winger.

Calgary Flames Could Trade Zach Whitecloud

The Calgary Flames have rebuilt their roster over the last two seasons by trading veterans for draft picks, prospects, and younger players.

They're expected to be sellers this season if they're out of playoff contention by the March 1 trade deadline.

Zach Whitecloud is currently the Flames' biggest trade chip. Acquired from the Vegas Golden Knights in January, the 29-year-old is a reliable defenseman with Stanley Cup experience. He has two years left on his contract with an affordable AAV of $2.8 million.

Kent Wilson of the Calgary Sun believes the Flames will retain Whitecloud this season to provide experience and leadership to their young defense corps. However, he doesn't rule out a trade if young blueliners Simon Nemec and Zayne Parekh step up this season.

Some observers still consider Whitecloud a suitable trade target this summer for clubs seeking a skillful, experienced top-four defenseman with a right-handed shot. The Toronto Maple Leafs and Montreal Canadiens have been suggested as suitors.

The Flames could move Whitecloud if their young defensemen show improvement this season. However, those promising youngsters will likely need another season to develop, meaning they'll need a seasoned hand like Whitecloud to help them.

Anaheim Ducks Could Make Cost-Cutting Trade to Sign Cutter Gauthier

The Anaheim Ducks were caught by surprise when center Leo Carlsson signed a five-year contract offer with the Philadelphia Flyers worth an average annual value of $18 million.

The Ducks matched the offer, but it left them with insufficient salary cap space to re-sign Cutter Gauthier.

A restricted free agent coming off an entry-level contract, Gauthier led the Ducks last season with 41 goals and 69 points. The 21-year-old winger reportedly rejected a four-year contract offer from the Ducks worth $14 million annually.

With $9.07 million in salary cap space , the Ducks must shed salary once Gauthier is signed. They'll get some short-term salary-cap relief by placing sidelined winger Troy Terry ($7 million AAV) on long-term injury reserve, but they must be cap-compliant when he's ready to return to the lineup.

Andre Leal of The Hockey News believes the Ducks must make a couple of cost-cutting trades . He suggested wingers Alex Killorn ($6.25 million AAV), Chris Kreider ($6.5 million), and Frank Vatrano ($4.6 million) as likely trade candidates.

If Gauthier has rejected $14 million annually, he won't accept anything within the Ducks' current remaining cap space. The Ducks are a rising team in the Western Conference and cannot afford to lose their leading goal scorer. Killorn, Kreider or Vatrano could be playing elsewhere later this season.

Minnesota Wild Can't Afford to Acquire Dylan Larkin

In early June, it was first reported that Dylan Larkin requested a trade. That made the 30-year-old Detroit Red Wings center a fixture in the rumor mill and appeared in our August NHL Trade Targets list.

Larkin has a full no-movement clause, but is reportedly willing to waive it for the Minnesota Wild, Vegas Golden Knights, Florida Panthers, and Dallas Stars.

According to MLive.com's Ansar Khan, the Wild were his preferred landing spot , but they might be unable to meet the Wings' asking price.

Khan stated the Red Wings sought, at minimum, a top-six forward (preferably a center) in return for Larkin. However, the Wild aren't parting with that type of asset, and Khan indicated the Red Wings aren't interested in a return of futures such as draft picks and prospects.

Wild followers aren't optimistic about their club's chances of landing Larkin. In a fan poll earlier this month by Michael Russo and Joe Smith of The Athletic, 68 percent of respondents didn't believe their team could acquire him, citing the club's limited trade capital.

The Wild don't have a top-six forward to spare, and their lack of a true first-line center is the reason they were linked to Larkin in the first place. Unless the Wings lower their price, the Wild must get creative, perhaps by getting a third team involved that has the assets that could interest Detroit.

Stats via NHL.com , salary cap and contract info via PuckPedia .

articles.title: Ranking the 5 Most Likely Men's WWE Money in the Bank 2026 Winners
articles.summary: Sunday Night's Main Event is the next big show for WWE on September 6, but the next official premium live event is Money in the Bank on October 10.
articles.body:
Sunday Night's Main Event is the next big show for WWE on September 6, but the next official premium live event is Money in the Bank on October 10.

The MITB event is usually one of the more anticipated PLEs on the calendar because the outcome isn't always as predictable as the average match. Plus, who doesn't love a good fight with ladders?

There are a lot of potential names who could end up in this year's men's Money in the Bank bout, but only a handful seem like possible winners.

Let's take a look at some of the most likely names to walk out of New Orleans with the briefcase.

Royce Keys has had slightly inconsistent booking lately, but it's clear WWE management sees him as a potential top star.

He might be new to the company, but the 17-year veteran is by no means a rookie, so it would make perfect sense for him to end up in this match.

The only thing that kept us from placing him higher on the list is the fact that he has not won a title in WWE yet, and it might be best to give him a run with the United States or Intercontinental Championship to see how he does.

Keys winning would immediately inject some new blood into the main event scene, which WWE sorely needs right now.

Finn Balor has talked a lot about wanting to get back into the hunt for a world title since coming to SmackDown, and this might be his way back into the chase.

Balor was the first-ever universal champion, but an injury during the title match in which he won the belt forced him to relinquish it before he ever got to defend it.

Now that he is free from The Judgment Day and back to his old babyface ways, it would be the perfect time to throw him into the title picture.

His popularity has been consistent, and Balor has always been a reliable performer in the ring, so there would be no downside to giving him the briefcase at this stage in his career.

Drew McIntyre has been out of action since losing to Jacob Fatu at WrestleMania 42, but if he is ready to come back, this would be the perfect time.

The MITB briefcase would make him even more dangerous than he already is, which is saying a lot because he is one of the most physically imposing members on the WWE roster.

Whether the Scot does it as a heel or babyface doesn't matter because his return would be cheered by fans either way, so WWE has some wiggle room with the kind of story it would tell with him holding the case.

The only downside to this scenario is that McIntyre won the briefcase in 2024, so having him repeat so soon might not be the best option.

WWE NXT Results, Winners, Live Grades, Reaction, Highlights Before Heatwave 2026

Trick Williams is currently involved in a feud with Baron Corbin over the United States Championship, but once that is done, it wouldn't be surprising to see WWE test him out in the main event scene.

It's no secret that WWE sees Trick as a valued member of the roster. He is booked strong, featured regularly and has a celebrity manager. His ascension has been quick but steady.

Putting the MITB briefcase in his hands would not be a bad idea at all. Even if he didn't successfully cash it in, having him circling the world title picture would be a great next step in his career.

If he ends up being booked in the match, we're giving him strong odds to win.

Solo Sikoa is definitely going to end up challenging Roman Reigns for the world title at some point, but he would be so much more dangerous with the MITB briefcase.

This would be a slam-dunk decision for WWE. Sikoa has built real momentum with the WWE Universe in recent months, and now is the time to capitalize.

Having him use the briefcase to defeat Reigns would also protect The Tribal Chief's character, which is something WWE seems intent on doing.

A few months of Sikoa parading around with the briefcase and taunting his cousin with it before finally cashing it in would be highly entertaining television.

Do we actually think Danhausen will win the Money in the Bank match? No, but there is an argument for why it would be great.

The beauty of his character is he is not driven by the same motivations as every other pro wrestler. Titles don't seem to be his top priority, so there is an easy comedic avenue to take.

Imagine Danhausen wins the case and then opens it to find a contract when he was expecting human monies. He would be the first person in WWE history to be mad about winning, but he could take advantage of the situation.

Having him attempt to auction the case off to the highest bidder would make for some hilarious segments, especially if someone unexpected ends up getting the case in the end.

Or, Danhausen could place a curse on the case so that whoever tried to cash it in fails miserably. There are multiple options for how to make this work.

This might not be the kind of decision every fan would enjoy, but if you like Danhausen, you would probably enjoy him running around with the briefcase for a while.

articles.title: Bayley Fuels WWE Rumors, New Reports on Joe Hendry and Ilja Dragunov's Exit amid AEW Buzz
articles.summary: Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.
articles.body:
Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.

Bayley Has Exchange with Pearce Amid WWE Absence

ESPN Addresses 'Completely False' Rumors About Future WWE Contract

Bayley has not been seen on WWE programming since last month, but she got fans talking Sunday after an exchange with Raw general manager Adam Pearce.

In response to an Instagram post (h/t Derek Holloway of Ringside News) by Bayley about her 10-year anniversary of getting called up to WWE's main roster, Pearce commented with clapping hands emojis.

Bayley responded by writing, "Hey, let's talk," to which Pearce replied, "You know where to find me."

The last time Bayley appeared on a televised WWE show was on July 18 when she lost to Lyra Valkyria at Saturday Night's Main Event.

She subsequently had two matches at WWE live events, but it has now been over a month since Bayley was part of WWE programming.

Bayley's absence comes amid a great deal of speculation regarding her pro wrestling future.

While the exact end date of Bayley's WWE contract is not publicly known, Bryan Alvarez of Wrestling Observer Radio (h/t WrestlingInc.com's Julien D'Alessandro ) reported earlier this month that he had heard her deal is up in January.

As is the case with any big WWE name who may be on the verge of free agency, some have theorized that Bayley could make the jump to AEW to reunite with longtime friend Mercedes Moné.

However, since Bayley's name has been mentioned often on WWE programming as of late, particularly by Valkyria, there is at least some belief that her WWE tenure may not be over yet.

Dave Meltzer of Wrestling Observer Radio (h/t Holloway ) recently offered his perspective, saying, "The frequent mentions of her on Raw this week would indicate to me that they expect her back. If they believed she might be leaving, they would not mention her name."

Bayley's exchange with Pearce could potentially be another clue that a return to WWE programming is possible, but anything could be on the table until and unless she resurfaces.

Reported Reason for Hendry's Recent WWE Hiatus

Joe Hendry's absence from WWE programming over the past few weeks is reportedly due to an outside-the-ring project he is working on for the company.

According to PWInsider.com (h/t Felix Upton of Ringside News), Hendry has a role in a live-action micro-drama for mobile platforms as part of WWE's partnership with ReelShort.

Prior to his hiatus, Hendry took part in a concert with Danhausen on the July 27 episode of Raw. However, they were interrupted and attacked by Judgment Day members Dominik Mysterio and JD McDonagh, as well as boxer Ryan Garcia.

At SummerSlam, Hendry showed up during the Human Monies on a Pole match between Danhausen and Mysterio, and he helped Danhausen pull off the victory.

The next night on Raw, Hendry lost decisively in a match against Bron Breakker, and he has not shown up on Raw since then.

Hendry was called up to WWE's main roster in April following a successful run in NXT that saw him hold the NXT Championship once.

While Hendry has not enjoyed that same level of success on Raw yet, the fact that WWE is using him for outside projects suggests that the company sees plenty of value in his skill set.

Rumors on Dragunov's Future After WWE Departure

Ilja Dragunov is reportedly being linked to AEW following the expiration of his WWE contract.

According to Fightful Select (h/t Steve Carrier of Ringside News), AEW sources have not yet heard about Dragunov joining the company, but other sources within pro wrestling expressed their belief that Dragunov ultimately will sign with AEW based on a "hunch."

PWInsider.com (h/t WrestlePurists ) first reported Saturday that Dragunov's WWE contract was expiring, leading to his exit from the company.

False Finish followed up by reporting that although WWE "would have liked Dragunov to stay with the company," he ultimately made the decision to leave.

Given that Dragunov's contract expired rather than him getting notified of a release, the typical 90-day non-compete clause does not apply to him.

That means Dragunov is a free agent and already free to work elsewhere at any time.

The 32-year-old Dragunov has long been regarded as one of the most physical and entertaining in-ring workers in pro wrestling, which led to some major accolades in WWE.

Dragunov was both an NXT United Kingdom and NXT champion before getting called up to the main roster and holding the United States Championship.

However, Dragunov's screen time took a major hit after he dropped the U.S. title to Carmelo Hayes in December, and he had not been seen on WWE programming since April prior to his departure.

If Dragunov and AEW do have mutual interest, it would perhaps behoove them to get a deal done quickly because he could show up next Sunday at the All In pay-per-view as a surprise entrant in the Casino Gauntlet match.

articles.title: Cambuur fans suffer burns as fireworks set off during Dutch league match
articles.summary: Game resumed despite injuries to home fans, but it would have been abandoned if a player or match official had been hit.
articles.body:
Dutch side SC Cambuur has said fans suffered burns, hearing damage and eye injuries after visiting Feyenoord supporters threw fireworks during a league match in Leeuwarden in the Netherlands province of Friesland.

The match on Sunday was halted for about 20 minutes in the first half when fans in the away section lit large numbers of red flares and threw fireworks.

Some were aimed towards sections of the ground containing Cambuur supporters, while one exploded on the pitch just a few metres from Feyenoord goalkeeper Tjark Ernst.

“Our own goalkeeper had a flare fired at him and only just managed to avoid it,” said Feyenoord general manager Robert Eenhoorn, describing the incident as “simply terrible”.

Cambuur said in a statement on Monday that five fans were confirmed to have been injured and that the club would work with the authorities to make sure those responsible were caught.

“It should be clear that setting off and firing fireworks is completely unacceptable and has no place in a football stadium whatsoever,” the club added.

Leeuwarden Mayor Foort van Oosten also condemned the incident and promised an investigation, while the Dutch football association said it would revisit its protocols for incidents of disorder.

The game resumed despite the injuries to the supporters, but it would have been abandoned if a player or match official had been hit.

“That doesn’t feel right,” Jan Bluyssen, KNVB manager of professional football competition affairs, told Dutch news agency ANP.

“We need to examine whether the protocol is still appropriate and how we might want to adjust it.”

Feyenoord won the match 5-2 to maintain their unbeaten start to the new league season, while newly promoted Cambuur have lost all three of their opening matches.

articles.title: Former NBA player Enes Kanter ejected after confrontation with WNBA’s Cloud
articles.summary: Kanter was ejected from the Indiana-Chicago WNBA game after he was confronted by Sky guard Natasha Cloud on court.
articles.body:
Former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom was ejected after a ‌verbal altercation with WNBA player Natasha Cloud of the Chicago Sky during the third quarter of Chicago’s loss to the visiting Indiana Fever.

Kanter Freedom, sitting ⁠courtside, stood up and took ⁠a few steps towards the court with his arms outstretched after Cloud began pointing and yelling at him at the start of an Indiana timeout on Sunday.

A game official and security personnel got between them, and her teammates pulled Cloud away. The official ⁠gestured for Kanter Freedom to be ejected, and he was escorted from his seat by team and arena security.

Kanter Freedom, 34, wore a black T-shirt that read: “WOMAN noun. Adult human female.”

Cloud, 34, spoke with team and league security after the Sky’s 113-90 loss but did not address the media. ⁠She did post a statement on social media, per CBS Sports.

“To every trans kid/person, You are a part of MY community & tribe. You belong. You’re loved. You’re seen. You’re perfect as you are. & you will always be protected by me,” Cloud wrote.

Kanter Freedom, who had a conversation with police officers before exiting Wintrust Arena, later wrote on his X account, “I just got kicked out of a @WNBA game for supporting WOMEN! Let that sink in, America.”

Sky coach Tyler ‌Marsh said at his postgame news conference that Cloud did not want to be a distraction.

“I told her she wasn’t,” Marsh said. “I told her we all embrace her as someone who protects our team and people who need to be protected. Tash is always gonna stand on that, and we stand for Tash.”

Marsh also had a message for spectators, apparently with Kanter Freedom in mind.

“There’s so many good things about this league and so many good things about the play of these players, that if you come to a game, you should probably come to enjoy the basketball,” Marsh said.

“That seems pretty simple to me. I think these players deserve that and have earned that. Being a ⁠former basketball player, you should probably understand and feel that, too.”

Kanter Freedom, formerly known as Enes Kanter, played ⁠centre for 11 years in the NBA for five teams from 2011-12 to 2021-22 and averaged 11.2 points, 7.8 rebounds and 21.5 minutes in 748 regular-season games (259 starts).

He also has spoken out on social issues, including the debate about transgender athletes. The WNBA, which has never had a known transgender player, has been ensnared in the issue, only heightened ⁠when the Fever’s Sophie Cunningham came out strongly in favour of women’s sports being solely for women.

Cunningham emphasised in her remarks last month in an ESPN profile that “girls should never have to compete with biological men”.

Cunningham later ⁠said on July 22 that she does not “dislike anyone” and that there is “room to love everyone”. She continued, “I’m ⁠also there to love biological women, and I think that there are rights that need to be protected. And, like I said, I’m gonna stand true to that. I’ll never falter in my beliefs in that. But I have never once stated that I hated the trans community.”

There have been rallies outside WNBA arenas involving people who are both pro-Cunningham and ‌anti-Cunningham.

Kanter Freedom and another former NBA player, Royce White, have talked about being eligible for the 2027 WNBA Draft, and both claim to now identify as women, according to media reports.

The league does not have a public policy about transgender participation. The collective bargaining agreement, signed in March, states ‌that “only ‌players who are women are eligible to play in the WNBA”.

Cloud is in her 11th season in the WNBA and first in Chicago. She entered Sunday averaging 11.4 points, 5.0 assists, 3.6 rebounds and 29.1 minutes in 36 games (23 starts).

She has also played for the Washington Mystics (2015-19, 2021-23), the Phoenix Mercury (2024) and the New York Liberty (2025).

articles.title: The walls appeared to be closing in on Gianni Infantino. Not everyone wants him gone
articles.summary: Former soccer great Samuel Eto’o exclusively told CNN Sports that he thinks FIFA President Gianni Infantino has done nothing wrong and wants the controversial FFE proposal back on the table for discussion.
articles.body: In recent weeks, it might have felt inevitable that Gianni Infantino would be forced to resign as FIFA president. The walls were closing in on him, and the rising tide of criticism following his failed attempt to rush through his controversial FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal seemed overwhelming. And yet, despite calls for him to step down still echoing around the sport, Infantino is still holding on to power with the FIFA presidential election fast approaching in March. And while some don’t want to wait that long to have the chance of toppling Infantino, the current FIFA boss does have some support swimming in the sea of objectors. One of those people is the president of the Cameroonian Football Federation (FECAFOOT) Samuel Eto’o, who recently told CNN Sports in an exclusive interview that Infantino hasn’t done anything wrong and actually called for the controversial plan that caused this tumultuous situation to be revisited. Eto’o was once one of the best players in the world, scoring countless goals and winning major trophies for the likes of Barcelona, Inter Milan, Chelsea and Real Madrid. He was elected FECAFOOT president in 2021 and has since set about growing the profile of both Cameroonian and African soccer as a whole. “I don’t think that President Gianni Infantino has done anything wrong,” Eto’o told CNN Sports when asked about the FIFA president’s conduct regarding the FFE plan. “I think the timing of all of that is because there’s an election coming out, when Gianni Infantino is standing. All of this has happened because there’s an election coming out, that’s all there is.” Eto’o’s voice will come as a welcome refuge for Infantino, who has been battered from pillar to post by a host of confederations. European body UEFA has threatened to boycott future tournaments, while the North & Central American and Caribbean governing body CONCACAF and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) demanded a change in leadership. The upcoming Under-20 Women’s World Cup in September could be the next flashpoint, with UEFA teams potentially not taking part. That would mean six of the qualified teams wouldn’t play, including the current host Poland. ‘Incredible’ FFE plan The Confederation of African Football (CAF) has been a rare backer of Infantino, although questions remain about which individual nations actually support its federation’s stance. Cameroon appears to be very much in line, and Infantino even name-checked Eto’o in a ‘thank-you post’ on Instagram last week. “President Gianni Infantino has changed football,” Eto’o added, urging fellow African nations to support the FIFA president. “He’s given opportunities to nations that didn’t have those opportunities to take part in the most beautiful tournament, the World Cup. He enabled smaller nations to get seats at these competitions. “He has helped our continent. He’s helped our federations to develop much more quickly, and we need to acknowledge that. We need to accept and recognize what he’s done, and we should support him for everything he’s done up to now.” Eto’o told CNN Sports the proposed plan would have helped distribute wealth in a fairer manner, allowing smaller nations to compete with the biggest in the world by having better facilities and resources. He said it would have helped teams like Cameroon to attract the best players in the world – such as Kylian Mbappé, who was born in France but who has Cameroonian heritage through his father. “There are federations in other continents that are in the same situation as us, that find themselves more or less at the same financial level as us to develop the football that we love so much. We want to see the (Lionel) Messis, we want to see the Mbappés, but I would like to see Mbappé play for Cameroon.” FIFA has already apologized for some of its actions and scrapped the FFE proposal. It also backed Infantino after a crisis meeting in Morocco last month. The narrative from FIFA now is that erroneous media reporting blew the proposed plans out of context, and that’s something echoed by Eto’o, who still thinks it was a good idea and hopes it can be debated if Infantino is reelected next year. “The bigger nations took up the media space. They gave their point of view, and President Gianni Infantino wanted to keep the family of football together, and he decided to withdraw the project,” he said. “I remain convinced that for us as Africans, this project was something that could have been incredible. It would have reset the balance of power in football to ensure that our talent doesn’t disappear and end up playing for other nations. “At the end of the day, those who have talked about the project and who’ve given their opinion haven’t properly read what it’s all about, and in some cases, they looked at it from their dominant position. He added: “I want to see all of my colleagues, all of the presidents, re-reading the project. After President Infantino is re-elected, we will have the strength to ask for this project to be put back on the table for discussion. “I remain convinced that, if there is a democratic vote, this project will be adopted because it’s good for the majority.” Support for Infantino Eto’o is not the only person banging the drum for Infantino in what’s become an increasingly fractured landscape. Support from CAF could be crucial, but there is also sympathy from other parts of the world. South America’s CONMEBOL has praised FIFA for scrapping its controversial plan but stopped short of calling for Infantino to resign. The Argentinian FA has also thrown its full weight behind the beleaguered leader. He also has support from Mexico (member of CONCACAF) and AFC members Qatar, Indonesia and the Philippines, showing how some national soccer associations are breaking away from the stance of their confederations. It’s a numbers game involving which of the 211 national associations are either for or against Infantino staying on. The election next year can’t come soon enough for some critics, although it’s not yet clear who would challenge Infantino – contenders need to come forward by the November 18 deadline. But there might be another way to push the leader out early. Should 20% of FIFA’s 211 member nations make a formal written request, an extraordinary congress would be called, as per FIFA’s statutes. A vote of no confidence in Infantino could then be launched, giving all members a chance to decide his fate – although CNN Sports could find no official guidelines about this potenital process. But for now, the FIFA president remains in post. And despite countless new criticisms emerging every day, there is belief from people such as Eto’o, that the leader can somehow stay on.

articles.summary: St Helens keep their play-off hopes alive with victory over Castleford, despite Jackson Hastings' sending off for violent conduct; his Grade E offence for punching the Tigers' Tyler Dupree carries a three-game ban, meaning his season could be over if Saints fail to qualify
articles.body:
Hastings was dismissed in the first half of the 36-12 victory after punching Castleford's Tyler Dupree, who was sin-binned for the same incident.

Commenting on Hastings' dismissal, Castleford director of rugby Chris Chester told Sky Sports : "Scott Murrell just jumped (in the way of Dupree). We all know the rules, you can't punch people in the face."

The win keeps Saints' play-off hopes alive, though they are currently on 28 points and seventh in the standings, one place outside of the play-off positions with three games to go.

articles.title: Four arrested over fatal shooting of South African boxer Zolani Tete
articles.summary: Tete, who won world WBF flyweight and WBO bantamweight titles, was killed outside his home in Eastern Cape last week.
articles.body:
South African police say they have arrested four people in connection with the murder of two-time boxing world champion Zolani Tete , who was shot last week.

The four suspects arrested over the weekend are aged between 22 and 28, police said in a statement on Monday. One has been formally charged with murder.

Tete won the IBF junior bantamweight world title in 2014 and the WBO bantamweight world title in 2017.

articles.title: Samuel Eto’o urges support for embattled FIFA President Gianni Infantino
articles.summary: Former star striker, now head of Cameroon’s FA, backs Infantino despite mounting pressure on him to resign.
articles.body:
Former Cameroon star Samuel Eto’o has thrown his support behind beleaguered FIFA President Gianni Infantino , saying he “hasn’t done anything wrong” despite facing mounting pressure to step down over a controversial World Cup selloff plan.

Infantino has come under intense scrutiny since the collapse of a proposal to secure private investment in FIFA tournaments, including the World Cup.

UEFA, which oversees European football, has threatened a boycott of FIFA competitions, with several continental and national federations also withdrawing their support for Infantino.

However, Eto’o, president of the Cameroonian Football Federation, dismissed criticism of Infantino’s leadership, suggesting the backlash was driven largely by political manoeuvring ahead of FIFA’s presidential election next year.

“I don’t think that President Gianni Infantino has done anything wrong,” the former Barcelona, Inter Milan and Chelsea striker told CNN.

“I think the timing of all of that is because there’s an election coming out.”

Infantino’s plan, which would reportedly have distributed substantial funding to FIFA’s 211 member associations, faced strong opposition from several confederations and was ultimately abandoned.

The FIFA president remains under pressure, with the possibility of a no-confidence vote being triggered. UEFA, the Asian Football Confederation (AFC), and the Confederation of North, Central American and Caribbean Association Football (CONCACAF) have all voiced concerns over FIFA’s direction in recent weeks.

But the Confederation of African Football (CAF) earlier this month “unanimously reconfirmed its support” for Infantino, and Eto’o’s backing is aligned with that position.

“President Gianni Infantino has changed football,” said Eto’o, urging fellow African countries to support the Swiss official.

“He’s given opportunities to nations that didn’t have those opportunities to take part in the most beautiful tournament, the World Cup. He enabled smaller nations to get seats at these competitions.

“He has helped our continent. He’s helped our federations to develop much more quickly, and we need to acknowledge that. We need to accept and recognise what he’s done, and we should support him for everything he’s done up to now.”

Meanwhile, a group of former international players, including World Cup winners and FIFA legends, called on Monday ⁠for immediate change at FIFA, saying its leadership under embattled Infantino had been blinded by power.

“We ‌share the exact same concerns as the millions of fans around the world,” said former players including France’s 1998 men’s World Cup winners Emmanuel Petit, Bixente Lizarazu and Robert Pires as well as American former women’s world champion Briana Scurry and former England international Lucy Bronze.

“Like them, we have watched the game we love drift away from its core values under FIFA’s current leadership. Change is necessary. Power has blurred the current leadership’s ability to distinguish between its own interests and what is best ⁠for football,” the group said.

The group also includes ⁠former Peru forward Claudio Pizarro, former Argentina international Juan Sebastian Veron, former Togo captain Emmanuel Adebayor, and FIFA legends Didier Drogba and David James.

FIFA legends are former players recognised for their contributions to the sport who help promote football on behalf of the ⁠global body, playing in exhibition matches and supporting social and charity projects worldwide.

“We call on all stakeholders to step forward and help reshape the future ⁠of our sport. There are good people within FIFA who want ⁠to rebuild trust, but a new era requires a structural change: a real, direct say for players and fans in how football is run,” the group said.

Infantino is up for re-election next year, but world football’s regional powerhouses are discussing whether to move a ‌vote of no confidence in him ahead of the ballot, senior figures familiar with the discussions told the Reuters news agency last week.

“Those who step onto the pitch and those who sit in the stands deserve a genuine ‌voice ‌to help reshape football’s future together. For the fans, for the players, and for the good of the game, we will be silent no more,” the players’ group said.

articles.title: England drop fast bowler Bryden Carse amid investigation into club incident
articles.summary: The 31-year-old Durham bowler will not play against Pakistan in the upcoming second Test match.
articles.body:
England fast bowler ‌Brydon Carse has been dropped from the squad for the second ⁠Test against ⁠Pakistan amid an investigation into an incident at a club in Derby, the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) has said.

“Following a ⁠referral from the ECB, the Cricket Regulator has confirmed that they will investigate events on Saturday night in Derby,” the board said in a statement on Monday.

“Brydon ⁠Carse will no longer be available for selection for the second men’s test while this investigation is ongoing and the full facts are obtained.”

Carse, who did not play in the opening test victory at Headingley, will be replaced by Sonny ‌Baker.

Videos circulated on social media appearing to show the 31-year-old Durham bowler in handcuffs being spoken to by police officers outside a venue. According to reports, Carse was not arrested and no charges were brought.

It has been a busy summer for England’s Cricket Regulator, the body set up to investigate matters where there is an allegation of a breach of ⁠the ECB’s code of conduct.

In June, it concluded an ⁠investigation into former test captain Ben Stokes and fast bowler Gus Atkinson after a nightclub incident following the first test against New Zealand.

Both were left out of the second test before ⁠the regulator ruled that there was insufficient evidence to establish that any regulatory breach occurred.

The latest investigation comes five ⁠days after England’s returning test captain Joe Root ⁠spoke of the players being “really good role models and human beings” following a series of incidents and accusations of a drinking culture.

Controversy has followed England recently, with off-field issues ‌during last winter’s tours – including Harry Brook being fined 30,000 pounds ($41,000) following an altercation in Wellington, New Zealand – as well as reports of drinking during a mid-Ashes series trip ‌to ‌Noosa.

Stokes retired from international cricket after returning for the third test against New Zealand and Brendon McCullum was sacked as test coach.

articles.title: Former snooker world champion Graeme Dott convicted of child sex abuse
articles.summary: The 49-year-old was found to have subjected a girl and a boy to multiple incidents of abuse.
articles.body:
Former snooker world champion Graeme Dott has been convicted of sexually abusing two children several decades ago in a trial in ⁠a Scottish court.

Dott was charged with two counts of “lewd, indecent and libidinous behaviour” ⁠against a girl from 1993 to 1996 and a boy from 2006 to 2010.

The indictment alleged that the 49-year-old had sexually assaulted the girl, ‌exposed himself to her and induced her to touch him. Dott was also accused of making sexual remarks to the boy and touching his genitals.

He denied the charges but was found guilty on Monday after a trial ⁠at the High Court ⁠in Glasgow. He will be sentenced next month.

“Dott is a dangerous individual, and I hope this conviction provides some ⁠measure of comfort to those impacted by his crimes,” Detective Inspector ⁠Gary Smillie from Police ⁠Scotland told reporters.

Dott won the world snooker championship in 2006, beating Peter Ebdon 18-14 in the final, and ‌finished as runner-up in 2004 and 2010.

He was suspended by the World Professional Billiards and ‌Snooker ‌Association after the charges were announced last year.
